title: Exact scalar multiplication gives a periodic K-flat resolution
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings; module sheaves mean [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $t$ be a global section of $\mathcal O$, meaning a family $t_U\in\mathcal O(U)$ compatible with every restriction, with $t_U^2=0$ for every object $U$. Let $\mu_t:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O$ be multiplication by $t$, and assume $\ker(\mu_t)=\operatorname{im}(\mu_t)$ as subobjects of $\mathcal O$. Put $E=\operatorname{coker}(\mu_t)$, with quotient map $\pi:\mathcal O\to E$. Define the cochain complex $P$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] by $P^i=\mathcal O$ for $i\leq0$, $P^i=0$ for $i>0$, $d_P^i=\mu_t$ for $i<0$, and all other differentials zero. The quotient map in degree zero and zero maps in other degrees define an augmentation $\varepsilon:P\to E[0]$. The augmented sequence $\cdots\xrightarrow{\mu_t}\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\mu_t}\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\pi}E\to0$ is exact. Moreover $H^0(P)\cong E$, $H^i(P)=0$ for $i\ne0$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], every term of $P$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and $\varepsilon$ is a K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For the one-point site and $\mathcal O=R$ a commutative ring, this is an augmented free resolution of $R/tR$ with basis $1$ in every nonpositive degree.

source.place: The examples: infinite periodic multiplication resolution; generalized to a square-zero scalar on a ringed site with kernel equal to image

proof.text: The compatibility of the sections $t_U$ with restriction makes $\mu_t$ a morphism of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Its square is zero: on every section $a$ it sends $a$ to $t_U^2a=0$. Consequently all consecutive differentials of $P$ compose to zero, including at the transition to the zero term in degree $1$; thus $P$ is a cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Since $\pi\mu_t=0$ by the cokernel definition, the degree-zero map $\pi$ and the zero components satisfy the chain-map equation, giving $\varepsilon:P\to E[0]$.

source.place: The examples, infinite periodic multiplication resolution

proof.text: For every $i<0$, both maps entering and leaving degree $i$ are $\mu_t$. The assumed equality $\ker\mu_t=\operatorname{im}\mu_t$ is exactly exactness at that term of the augmented sequence. Equivalently the cohomology formula of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives $H^i(P)=\ker\mu_t/\operatorname{im}\mu_t=0$. These are equalities of subobjects in the abelian category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; no sectionwise surjectivity or enough-points hypothesis is being assumed.

source.place: The examples, infinite periodic multiplication resolution

proof.text: At the last copy of $\mathcal O$, the cokernel quotient $\pi$ is an epimorphism with kernel $\operatorname{im}\mu_t$, giving exactness of $\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\mu_t}\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\pi}E\to0$ in the abelian category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Because $d_P^0=0$, the formula of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] identifies $H^0(P)=\mathcal O/\operatorname{im}\mu_t=E$; the induced map $H^0(\varepsilon)$ is precisely this quotient identification. All terms in degrees $i>0$ vanish, so $H^i(P)=0$ there. Since $E[0]$ has $E$ in degree zero and zero cohomology elsewhere, these computations show that $H^i(\varepsilon)$ is an isomorphism for every $i$, hence $\varepsilon$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: The examples, infinite periodic multiplication resolution

proof.text: For any module sheaf $\mathcal F$, the sectionwise maps $\mathcal F(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O(U)}\mathcal O(U)\to\mathcal F(U)$, $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$, have inverse $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Their composites are identities by the tensor balancing relation, and both commute with restrictions. Sheafifying the presheaf tensor as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] therefore gives a natural isomorphism $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O\cong\mathcal F$. Also $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}0=0$ since its sectionwise tensor is zero. Thus tensoring with $\mathcal O$ or $0$ is, respectively, the identity or zero functor and preserves exact sequences. Both are flat by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], so every term of $P$ is flat.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), displayed sheafified tensor definition; Tag 03ER (definition-flat), item (3)

proof.text: The complex $P$ is bounded above with bound $0$ and its terms are flat by Step 4. Apply [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], whose statement is for arbitrary ringed sites, to conclude that $P$ is K-flat. Together with the quasi-isomorphism $\varepsilon$ from Step 3 this is exactly a K-flat resolution of $E[0]$ as defined in [def-pc-kflat-complex].

On the one-point site with ring $R$, module sheaves are ordinary $R$-modules. The image of multiplication by $t$ is the ideal $tR$, so $E=R/tR$. Each nonzero-position term $P^i=R$ for $i\le0$ is free on the singleton basis $1$: the coefficient map $R\to R$, $r\mapsto r\cdot1$, is the identity. The augmentation is the ordinary quotient map and exactness was proved in Steps 2--3. This gives the stated augmented free resolution, with every differential before the augmentation multiplication by $t$.
